summary.short: Sets EU rules giving users of connected products and related services access to the data they generate, and requiring data holders to share it with users and their chosen third parties. Also governs B2B data sharing terms, public-sector emergency access and cloud switching. Applies from 12 September 2025.
summary.long: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 sets harmonised rules on fair access to and use of data. Article 1 covers product and related service data, data holders making data available to recipients, public-sector access in exceptional need, cloud switching and interoperability standards. This part covers Chapters I to III and only the heading of Chapter IV. Chapter II requires manufacturers and related-service providers to design products so that data are accessible to users by default (Art. 3), requires pre-contract information (Art. 3(2)-(3)), and obliges data holders to make readily available data accessible to users and, on request, to third parties (Arts. 4-5). This is subject to trade-secret safeguards (Art. 4(6)-(8)), a bar on users using data to build a competing connected product (Art. 4(10)), and exclusion of designated gatekeepers as eligible third parties (Art. 5(3)). Third parties must process data only for agreed purposes and may not profile except where strictly necessary (Art. 6). Microenterprises and small enterprises are partly exempt (Art. 7). Chapter III sets fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms for B2B data sharing (Art. 8), compensation limited to costs for SMEs (Art. 9), certified dispute settlement bodies (Art. 10), and technical protection measures and remedies (Art. 11). Personal data may be shared only where a valid GDPR legal basis exists. Enforcement in this part is limited to complaints to designated competent authorities; penalty provisions and the Chapters on public-sector access, cloud switching and interoperability are not in this part.

‘data’ means any digital representation of acts, facts or information
‘non-personal data’ means data other than personal data;
‘personal data’ means personal data as defined in Article 4, point (1), of Regulation (EU) 2016/679;
‘connected product’ means an item that obtains, generates or collects data concerning its use or environment
‘related service’ means a digital service, other than an electronic communications service, including software
‘processing’ means any operation or set of operations which is performed on data or on sets of data
‘data processing service’ means a digital service that is provided to a customer and that enables ubiquitous and on-demand network access
‘same service type’ means a set of data processing services that share the same primary objective, data processing service model and main functionalities;
‘data intermediation service’ means data intermediation service as defined in Article 2, point (11), of Regulation (EU) 2022/868;
‘data subject’ means data subject as referred to in Article 4, point (1), of Regulation (EU) 2016/679;
‘user’ means a natural or legal person that owns a connected product
‘data holder’ means a natural or legal person that has the right or obligation, in accordance with this Regulation
‘data recipient’ means a natural or legal person, acting for purposes which are related to that person’s trade, business, craft or profession
‘product data’ means data generated by the use of a connected product that the manufacturer designed to be retrievable
‘related service data’ means data representing the digitisation of user actions or of events related to the connected product
‘readily available data’ means product data and related service data that a data holder lawfully obtains or can lawfully obtain
‘trade secret’ means trade secret as defined in Article 2, point (1), of Directive (EU) 2016/943;
‘trade secret holder’ means a trade secret holder as defined in Article 2, point (2), of Directive (EU) 2016/943;
‘profiling’ means profiling as defined in Article 4, point (4), of Regulation (EU) 2016/679;
‘making available on the market’ means any supply of a connected product for distribution, consumption or use on the Union market
‘placing on the market’ means the first making available of a connected product on the Union market;
‘consumer’ means any natural person who is acting for purposes which are outside that person’s trade, business, craft or profession;
‘enterprise’ means a natural or legal person that, in relation to contracts and practices covered by this Regulation, is acting for purposes
‘small enterprise’ means a small enterprise as defined in Article 2(2) of the Annex to Recommendation 2003/361/EC;
‘microenterprise’ means a microenterprise as defined in Article 2(3) of the Annex to Recommendation 2003/361/EC;
‘Union bodies’ means the Union bodies, offices and agencies set up by or pursuant to acts adopted on the basis of the Treaty on European Union
‘public sector body’ means national, regional or local authorities of the Member States and bodies governed by public law of the Member States
‘public emergency’ means an exceptional situation, limited in time, such as a public health emergency
‘customer’ means a natural or legal person that has entered into a contractual relationship with a provider of data processing services
‘virtual assistants’ means software that can process demands, tasks or questions
‘digital assets’ means elements in digital form, including applications, for which the customer has the right of use
‘on-premises ICT infrastructure’ means ICT infrastructure and computing resources owned, rented or leased by the customer
‘switching’ means the process involving a source provider of data processing services, a customer of a data processing service
‘data egress charges’ means data transfer fees charged to customers for extracting their data through the network
‘switching charges’ means charges, other than standard service fees or early termination penalties, imposed by a provider of data processing services on a customer
‘functional equivalence’ means re-establishing on the basis of the customer’s exportable data and digital assets, a minimum level of functionality
‘exportable data’, for the purpose of Articles 23 to 31 and Article 35, means the input and output data, including metadata
‘smart contract’ means a computer program used for the automated execution of an agreement or part thereof
‘interoperability’ means the ability of two or more data spaces or communication networks
‘common specifications’ means a document, other than a standard, containing technical solutions
‘harmonised standard’ means a harmonised standard as defined in Article 2, point (1)(c), of Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012

An exceptional need to use certain data within the meaning of this Chapter shall be limited in time and scope and shall be considered to exist only in any of the following circumstances:
A contractual term is unfair if it is of such a nature that its use grossly deviates from good commercial practice in data access and use, contrary to good faith and fair dealing.

A contractual term shall be considered to be unilaterally imposed within the meaning of this Article if it has been supplied by one contracting party and the other contracting party has not been able to influence its content despite an attempt to negotiate it.
Each Member State shall designate one or more competent authorities to be responsible for the application and enforcement of this Regulation (competent authorities).
